units.author: retired_teacher
units.text: Found on the Lisle school beach this morning: a blue plastic fish box stamped with a Gilliver merchant's name, three lengths of good rope, and a single oar, painted green. The oar may belong to the missing rowing boat. I've put it in the school porch, where the caretaker has promised not to use it as a goalpost.

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: That oar's Jamie's right enough, he painted both of them green so folk would stop borrowing them. Fish box is the merchant's, they wash up after every blow, keep it for kindling. I'll fetch the oar next time I'm over Lisle way. Boat's still missing.

units.author: lineman_tess
units.text: Seth, how long can the boat's genset carry the terminal if the shore supply goes? Asking for the standby log, so I know who to ring first. Garvey says 'Seth, then the co-op, then your mum', but I think he's joking about the order.

units.author: ferry_engineer_seth
units.text: All night if it has to, Tess, she's got a full day tank. It's the berth lights and the waiting room heaters mostly. Ring me first, yes, Garvey's order is right. Your mum second is a bit harsh on the co-op though.

units.author: lh_dockguard_coriveth
units.text: Update. IT came this afternoon and took the recorder for monitor 4 away for testing. Running monitor 4 direct to the spare screen tonight, no recording. Northeast corner empty at 00:30 and 01:30. Patrolled, nil found. I miss the recorder, honestly. A screen you can't rewind makes you look harder.

units.author: lh_security_st
units.text: Break: Control brought doughnuts, which has never happened in six years, so either it's his birthday or somebody's getting sacked. Car park empty tonight apart from two cars that are always there and a shopping trolley that's been in bay 40 since the storm. I've named it. Its name is Gerald, after the binaural head on LowBand.

units.author: dc_3_wendell
units.text: If the plumber had asked, I would have told him which bays are visitors' bays, which is all I would have done. I have nothing against plumbers. The boiler on 4 is the only thing in this building that has been mended promptly this year, and I'm told it was mended by a man parked in my bay.

units.author: dc_8_benedikt
units.text: Thank you Tobin. I will not walk, but I can give you my satchel for the control, so the rail knock is the same as on my file. Then you can count it and remove it, like before. I think this is fair. I will be in the shop with Hassan while you do it.

units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: HM's right. I've had two lads in the chandlery today asking to hire a dinghy to go across and have a look at the camp. no. it's a working site and they're working. if you want to see the lights, stand on the front like everyone else.

units.author: skeptic_planner
units.text: Thank you, Bernard. Update on the yellow wellington: a small boy and his grandmother came past the noticeboard this afternoon and he identified it with great confidence and some tears. The case is closed. I mention it only because this thread has had a better week than most of the others.

units.author: lineman_tess
units.text: Thank you. Writing it down is all I needed. I've copied your minute log into my standby notes next to the trip times so they sit side by side. I'm not drawing conclusions either. I just want somebody to have the two lists together, in case it happens again.

units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, thanks, I've taken the fuel and oil figures from the site log. I've put six drums on tomorrow's boat, mostly saw fuel, plus two boxes of chain oil and a spare starter cord. If you need anything else, it has to be with me by 14:00. The charter skipper has asked for someone on the landing to take his lines. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: a short one from the car park
units.author: sam
units.text: quick one, waiting for Bea at drama club. her teacher says she's the loudest tree she's ever directed, which I'm choosing to take as praise. Mum rang three times today about the hospital parking. I've written down the code for the barrier on my hand. anyway, I'll write properly later if I'm still awake. S x

units.author: grieve_payroll
units.text: This is an automated message. Statement reference GLS-PS-1703 has been issued to all workers on contract KH-30 at their registered addresses. Workers without an email address will receive a paper copy at the next supply delivery. No action is required by the site lead. This mailbox is not monitored.

units.author: grieve_payroll
units.text: This is an automated reminder (repeat 2). The register for contract KH-30 continues to show crew wages outstanding. Status: OUTSTANDING. Settlement is made at the site terminal. Operations have been notified of the repeat. This notice will repeat daily. Do not reply; this mailbox is not monitored.

units.title: Timesheet closes tonight
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, a gentle nudge: the payroll timesheet window closes at 23:59 tonight. If the site log is up to date I can confirm it from here, so there's nothing for you to do unless the attendance is wrong. If it is wrong, please note the correction in the log before dark, as I won't see it until morning otherwise. Thanks, Ruth

units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, the charter skipper rang to say he's back at Gilliver and everything on the list went ashore. He mentioned the camp looked 'very tidy', which from him is high praise. Next run in four days unless you need something sooner. Thanks, Ruth

units.author: met
units.text: Tides and sea, Marrow Sound. High water Gilliver 05:31 and 17:56, height 3.9 m, tides falling toward neaps. Swell west 1.5 m this morning, decreasing to 1 m. Sea temperature 10 C. Small-craft advisory cancelled at 06:00. Mariners should still expect floating storm debris in the Gilliver channel.

units.title: Priority services: please register
units.author: power
units.text: Sound Power Co-op. With further night interruptions possible on the Gilliver and Brackwater coastal lines, we are asking customers who rely on powered medical equipment, or who are elderly or living alone, to join our free priority services register. Registered customers receive a call before planned work and a check-in call during longer outages. Family members may register on someone's behalf.

units.author: hist_wiki_marsh
units.text: Talk note, in reply. Pell's point about the ledger is fair and I'll stop restoring the phrase until we have looked. For the record, the society believes the camp's wage ledger survives, in a box of Coad family papers not yet catalogued. Until it is read, 'reasons not recorded' is perhaps more accurate than either 'unknown' or 'pay'. I've changed the article to that. Marsh.

units.author: naturalist_1923
units.text: Day 5. Walked the whole eastern shore, high water to the ridge. No deer sign whatever, as before; no rabbit either, which is odder. Badger setts: none. Mice and voles plentiful. [Sketch: the fish-curing house, roofless.] The boatman, asked again why the deer will not cross, said only that 'they've more sense'. I record this as a boatman's remark and not as natural history.
